extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers of archaeological methods papers (esp. network-analysis/preprint submissions) and PCI Archaeology recommenders
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and recommendation of an archaeology preprint that introduces a methodological innovation (Similarity Network Fusion) and a regional case study; guidance covers novelty, methods, reproducibility, data/figures, interpretation, and editorial issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and relevance of method
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper introduce a method new to archaeology (here SNF) and demonstrate its potential to offer new perspectives on existing data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show why the method is noteworthy for archaeology (e.g., SNF typically used in genomics but applicable to heterogenous/noisy archaeological datasets). Demonstrate potential through an instructive case study and discuss other possible archaeological applications (archaeobotany, archaeozoology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of prior work / literature grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: Author should demonstrate a deep and thorough understanding of previous investigations concerning material and similarity networks and situate the new approach in that literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant comparative studies (e.g., Habiba et al. 2018, Brainerd-Robinson discussions) and explicitly state how the approach extends or differs from earlier work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and justification of analytical decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical choices (similarity indices, clustering methods, cutoffs, thresholds, spectral algorithm parameters) must be made explicit and justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly explain what methods do in accessible terms; justify chosen clustering/detection thresholds; clarify why particular similarity coefficients were chosen and how alternatives compare; document decisions in Methods so readers can evaluate appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility of code and ability to replicate results
rubrics_metrics.description: Code should be runnable by reviewers/readers. The reviewer reran the provided Python code and expects it to work given clear instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide installation instructions (e.g., how to install snfpy), conda/environment details, explicit package versions, README with usage notes, additional comments in code for key steps, and clear header comments describing inputs/outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability and metadata completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Data used in analysis (csv files, site coordinates, attribute files, output matrices) should be shared with clear metadata describing variables and columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include files with site coordinates (or jittered coordinates if sensitive), full descriptions of variable/column headers (Individuals file clarity), and provide output files with clusters and unscaled similarities for each period/dataset to allow alternative checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of spatial/visual analysis and how correlations were assessed
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming spatial correlations (e.g., clusters correlate with sex, objects per grave, chronology), the methods used to assess those correlations must be explicit (visual inspection vs. statistical test) and reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether observations came from map visual inspection or statistical tests; describe any spatial correlation analysis procedures; report test statistics, degrees of freedom, p-values, and explain interpretation (e.g., ANOVA results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical reporting and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical results must be accurately reported and interpretations consistent (e.g., reporting F(1,44)=3.23, p<0.008 and reconciling apparent contradictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check numerical results and ensure textual claims match statistics; clarify seemingly contradictory statements and be cautious about overstating significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear link between aims/questions and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion and conclusion should synthesize findings and explicitly address the original aims (e.g., what the study teaches about cultural/ritual structuration and relationships between graves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit how the results answer the research questions and how the case study informs methodological potential for the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualisation of case study
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide adequate background on the case study area, cultural and ritual context, and why the chosen region/time periods are relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a concise contextual paragraph in the Introduction or Data section describing landscape, known burial practices, and how the method may fill knowledge gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality, clarity, and readability of figures and visualisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures must be legible (resolution, edge weights, colors), captions comprehensive, and use consistent color/legend conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure image resolution supports edge visibility; consider increasing edge thickness; list topological clusters in relevant captions; fix inconsistent color listings; correct commas and phrasing in captions; avoid overloading with too many color images but keep necessary network visualisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate figure design choices and explanation of display thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Choices such as 'restricted the representation to the 25 highest similarities' must be accurate (edges vs nodes) and explained so readers understand what the visualisations represent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct wording (edges vs nodes), explain thresholding/rescaling/plotting decisions (e.g., 25 highest connections, rescaling), and provide alternative lower-threshold visualisations in supplement if informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials and summary tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supplemental summary tables (e.g., grave goods, monument type, cluster membership) and files that aid interpretation and replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a comprehensive supplement or data annex with tabular summaries by cluster, final cluster outputs, and per-site attribute tables to support claims in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological transparency about preprocessing and data selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain data selection criteria, preprocessing steps, potential biases, and how datasets were constructed (e.g., two datasets choice rationale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document selection rationale, cleaning steps, how measurements were aggregated, handling of multiple burials, and consider showing summary tables of variable distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention and discussion of alternative similarity measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss advantages and disadvantages of other potential similarity measures (e.g., Brainerd-Robinson, cosine similarity) and cite relevant comparative literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add references (e.g., Habiba et al. 2018), and briefly comment on when SNF improves over commonly used coefficients and when it might not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software and environment specification
rubrics_metrics.description: State which software packages and versions were used (e.g., Python version, ArcGIS Pro), and any steps taken in other software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List versions, scripts used, describe ArcGIS rescaling/plotting choices or provide alternative scripts so readers without ArcGIS can replicate outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication-friendly outputs for spatial results
rubrics_metrics.description: If site location data are sensitive, provide jittered coordinates or otherwise enable spatial replication of mapping/cluster-location analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exact coordinates cannot be shared, include approximated/jittered locations and/or the output cluster assignments and mapping scripts so full replication of the main spatial claims is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious interpretation and discussion of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about limitations (small sample sizes, context-dependence) and avoid over-claiming; reconcile contradictory results across datasets/time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how sample size affects results and interpretation; qualify generality of spatial clusters and correlations; avoid language that contradicts statistical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript clarity, language, and organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing should be clear, direct, and polished; section ordering should foreground key analytic sections; fix wording and typographical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise for direct sentences, check consistency (e.g., 'aspatial' vs 'a spatial'), correct typos and confusing sentences, reorganize figure-text order so sections start with text rather than figures where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and completeness of references and bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference list must include all cited works and be consistently formatted without typographical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each in-text citation appears in bibliography (e.g., Brughmans 2010), correct typos in titles and author names, verify duplicate/identical DOIs are handled correctly, and fix spacing/punctuation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial and ethical disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare conflicts of interest and funding transparently in accordance with PCI code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit conflict of interest statement and funding statement (e.g., Swiss Study Foundation), and ensure authors comply with PCI policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to reviewers and revision transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Author should respond to reviewer comments, implement suggested changes where appropriate, and document major revisions in an Author's Reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear Author's Reply summarising changes (metadata, README, additional files, text clarifications), and note which suggestions were implemented or not and why.
